head_falling_away.name: Head Falling Away to Off-Side
head_falling_away.why_it_hurts: When your head falls over to the off-side or leg-side, your eyeline tilts and your hands follow your head away from the true line of the ball, causing leading edges to slip/gully or slicing the ball in the air.
head_falling_away.fix: Lead into the drive with your head, keeping your eyes level and chin tucked directly over the line of your front knee.
head_falling_away.drill: Drop-Ball Target Driving: Have a partner drop a ball from shoulder height onto a marked target; step forward and drive while holding your head dead still over the bounce for 2 seconds.

front_elbow_dropping.name: Front Elbow Dropping / Collapsed Arm
front_elbow_dropping.why_it_hurts: A collapsed or dropping front elbow forces the bottom hand to dominate, scooping the ball in the air towards extra cover or mid-off instead of stroking it along the carpet.
front_elbow_dropping.fix: Point your front elbow directly at the mid-off/cover region throughout the downswing, letting the top hand guide the stroke.
front_elbow_dropping.drill: Top-Hand Only Tee Drives: Place the ball on a batting tee; remove your bottom hand completely and stroke 25 consecutive cover drives focusing on keeping the front elbow high and dominant.

bat_across_the_line.name: Bat Coming Across the Line / Slicing
bat_across_the_line.why_it_hurts: Swinging outside-in across the trajectory of the ball reduces the sweet-spot impact zone, exposing the outside edge to slips and losing all power transfer.
bat_across_the_line.fix: Bring the bat down smoothly from first/second slip, presenting the full face straight through the line to extra cover.
bat_across_the_line.drill: Two-Stump Channel Drill: Place two upright cones or stumps 1.5 feet apart along the cover drive corridor; swing your bat through the channel without touching either marker.

short_stride_reach.name: Front Foot Not to the Pitch of the Ball
short_stride_reach.why_it_hurts: Reaching with your hands away from your body without committing your front foot leaves you lunging, playing with an angled bat away from your eyes.
short_stride_reach.fix: Commit a positive stride toward the line and bounce of the ball, planting your front toe pointing in the direction you want to hit.
short_stride_reach.drill: Shadow Step & Freeze: Mark foot placement spots with chalk; practice taking a positive stride towards cover, landing heel-first then rolling onto the front sole while keeping your weight balanced.

balance_loss_follow_through.name: Loss of Balance on Follow-Through
balance_loss_follow_through.why_it_hurts: Toppling off-balance immediately after impact indicates you rushed the shot with upper body torque rather than a solid front knee base, giving poor control.
balance_loss_follow_through.fix: Hold your finish! Freeze in your follow-through position like a photograph until the ball has traveled 20 yards.
balance_loss_follow_through.drill: 3-Second Pose Hold: After executing every drive, hold your finishing stance on your flexed front knee for a full 3 count without wobbling or moving your back toe.

bottom_hand_takeover.name: Bottom Hand Squeezing / Domination
bottom_hand_takeover.why_it_hurts: Tightening the bottom hand rolls the wrists prematurely or fliffs the ball aerially, diminishing placement precision.
bottom_hand_takeover.fix: Relax your bottom hand grip: use only thumb and index finger (a 'V' grip) while letting your top hand grip firmly.
bottom_hand_takeover.drill: Loose Grip Check Drill: Practice front-foot push-drives gripping the handle with your bottom hand's thumb and index finger only, driving cleanly past mid-off.
